Matchbook Learning Morning Meeting · K–2 Behavior Toolkit · Gentle Hands07

Slide 1 · Title & Promise R2

Hold up both open hands, palms out, and wiggle the fingers. “These are my hands. Today we learn how our hands keep our friends safe. Show me your hands.” Wait until every hand is up before moving on.

Look for

  • Every student shows open hands
  • Eyes on the slide or on you

If it breaks

  • Silly hands: model again, slowly and silently, then invite them back. No lecture.

Support adult

  • Sit beside any student who has had a hard morning; keep this lesson warm, not corrective

Language support

  • “Gentle” is new for many students: say it while softly patting your own arm
  • Spanish: suave · Kreyòl: dous

Engagement move Equity stick: pull one name and ask, “Show me gentle hands.” Any calm open hands earns praise.

Tier note: teach this before trouble, not the morning after a hitting incident in this room. If a child was hit today, wait a day. Never cast a real student as the child in the story.

Slide 2 · Regulate · Get Calm First R1

Model the gesture with them every time. “Smell the flower. Blow out the candle. Long and slow. Three times.” Do it with the class, not from the front.

Look for

  • Exhale longer than inhale
  • Shoulders drop
  • Gesture copied

If it breaks

  • If silliness: model silently once, then invite them back.

Support adult

  • Breathe audibly beside any student who cannot settle

Language support

  • No language demand; gesture carries it
  • Same two gestures used in every K–2 lesson

Engagement move LiveSchool: award a point to a student who breathes all three times with you. Name the behavior: “You breathed slow three times.”

Slide 3 · Orient · The Story R2, R3

Point to each picture as you tell it. “Malik was mad. He hit Nadege. Ouch! Nadege got hurt and felt sad. Malik could use gentle hands. Then everyone can play safe and have fun.” Then have the class say together: “Hitting hurts. We use gentle hands.”

Look for

  • Students follow the pictures in order
  • Whole class repeats the We say line

If it breaks

  • If students laugh at the hurt picture: pause, point to Nadege’s face, ask “How does her face look?”

Support adult

  • Point to each panel as the teacher narrates

Language support

  • Four pictures, three words each; numbers carry the order
  • Act out “Ouch” by holding your own arm

Engagement move Equity stick: “Which picture shows gentle hands? Point.” Pointing is a full answer.

Keep the focus on what Malik can do next time. He is learning, just like us.

Slide 4 · Connect · Turn and Talk R3, R4

Show knee to knee with a student partner. “Turn knee to knee. Look at Nadege. Tell your partner: She feels ___.” Give 30 seconds, then ring back.

Look for

  • Partners face each other
  • Most students say “sad” or point to the sad face
  • Partners take turns

If it breaks

  • If a pair is stuck: kneel in and say the stem with them.
  • If partners argue: “Take turns. You go first, then you.”

Support adult

  • Pair any student who needs support with a steady partner before the lesson starts

Language support

  • Pointing to a face is a complete answer
  • Spanish: triste · Kreyòl: tris

Engagement move Equity stick: call two names to share. Praise the frame: “You said: She feels sad. Full sentence!”

Slide 5 · Practice · Watch Me, Then Show Me R3, R4, R5

Read the scene. “A friend takes my truck. I feel mad. I can…” Invite one student to model: show a mad face, then pick a calm move from the row and do it. Narrate what you see and ask the class, “What did they do?” Then the whole class practices together.

Look for

  • A student models a mad face and then a calm move
  • Class names the calm move
  • Whole class rehearses deep breaths and “Can I have a turn?”

If it breaks

  • Excellent model: “Show the class again. Everyone, what calm move did you see?”
  • Partly right model: “You showed the mad face. Now show us the calm move. Try again.”
  • Silly model: “Thank you. Let’s see it the safe way.” Call a new student; no commentary.

Support adult

  • Stand near the calm corner so students can point to the real one

Language support

  • Five pictures; students can point instead of naming
  • Model “Can I have a turn?” as a sentence everyone says

Engagement move LiveSchool: award the student model a point for showing a calm move. Name it out loud.

Students model, not the teacher. The teacher narrates and asks the class what they saw.

Slide 6 · Commit · My Promise Today R2, R5

Put your hand on your heart. “Say it with me: I use gentle hands.” Then: “Point to the calm move you will use today when you feel mad.”

Look for

  • Every student says the promise
  • Every student points to one choice

If it breaks

  • If a student does not choose: offer two pictures and let them point.

Support adult

  • Notice and name a student’s promise later in the day

Language support

  • Hand on heart carries the promise
  • Spanish: Uso manos suaves · Kreyòl: Mwen sèvi ak men dous

Engagement move Equity stick: pull three names: “Which one did you pick?” Pointing counts.

Slide 7 · Transition · How We Leave R1, R4, R5

“How we leave is how we start our learning. Stand up. Gentle hands. Walk. Ready to learn. Let’s practice.” Do not time this at K–2.

Look for

  • Hands to self while moving
  • Calm walking, not rushing

If it breaks

  • “Let’s try that again. Back to your spot.” Rebuild clean, no commentary on individuals.

Support adult

  • Stand at the destination, not behind the group

Language support

  • Four icons, four words
  • No timing pressure at this age

Engagement move LiveSchool: award a point to the table that walks with gentle hands the whole way.

Gentle hands all day: look for it at centers, in line, and at recess, and name it when you see it.
